profile.reading: Per QTS own site, this Ashburn-Shellhorn DC2 facility (ASH3 DC2) is located at 22271 Shellhorn Rd, Ashburn, VA 20147, part of a 25 acre campus with 80 MW+ critical campus capacity across 2 buildings. Per-building square footage and MW allocation are not published.
profile.capacity_note: Part of a 25 acre, 2-building campus with 80 MW+ total critical capacity (per operators own site); campus total, not per-building
profile.research_note: Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 21 (mega-operator no-sources-key gap, QTS Loudoun/Prince William/GA/OH campus pass): added address and campus capacity from the operators own site. research_status remains complete.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Northern Virginia campus, spanning Loudoun County (Ashburn-Shellhorn, Ashburn-Moran, Ashburn Lockridge buildings), Prince William County (Manassas DC1, DC2, DC5), and Sterling (Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2). Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Ashburn-Shellhorn DC2 is one building within a 25-acre QTS campus in Loudoun County with 80 MW of published critical capacity across two buildings. The per-building allocation is not published, so the IT load available to this specific facility cannot be determined from QTS's specifications. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 80 MW across the full campus would support roughly 2000 racks, but this figure describes two buildings combined and establishes only an upper bound for any single facility.

This campus sits in Loudoun County, which hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, only 23 of which publish power consumption figures. The campus's 80 MW places it outside Virginia's top 23 published facilities by capacity, ranking 24th statewide among disclosed figures. Virginia's 23 published sites total 1375.4 MW, making this campus a modest contributor to the state's inventory by disclosed metrics.

QTS operates a seven-building footprint across Loudoun and Prince William counties and sterling, with multiple facilities in the Northern Virginia cluster. The operator publishes consolidated campus capacity rather than per-building specifications, which limits visibility into how much compute density any single structure can support. Whether this site matters to large-scale AI training depends on unpublished details: the split of 80 MW between two buildings, the power supply headroom, and the available rack space.
